To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose the Positive Example Based learning (PEBL) for Web page classification and introduce a novel algorithm Mapping-Convergence (MC) that achieves the classification accuracy as high as that achieved by traditional SVM (with both positive and negative training data).

we propose a novel approach called PEBL for Web page classification, that we show that the M-C algorithm is an effective algorithm to achieve the PEBL goal, and that we show that our PEBL framework can achieve classification accuracy as high as traditional SVM.

(1) PEBL framework can eliminate the need for manually constructing negative examples in Web page classification, (2) the M-C algorithm can achieve classification accuracy comparable to that of traditional SVM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to construct a classifier with positive examples only, without collecting negative examples.

two main contributions: (1) a novel framework, PEBL, for Web page classification that eliminates the need for collecting negative training examples and (2) a novel algorithm, M-C, that achieves classification accuracy comparable to traditional SVM with positive and negative data.
two important problems of Web page classification: (1) the need for negative training examples, and (2) the lack of labeled data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our M-C algorithm can achieve the same level of classification accuracy as traditional SVM, but without the need of negative training examples.
our proposed PEBL framework can be used to build classifiers without the need for collecting negative training examples.
PEBL is a promising framework to construct a classifier for a user-interesting Web page class.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a new learning framework for classification that eliminates the need for negative examples.
the PEBL framework is a new approach for Web page classification that eliminates the laborious work of collecting negative training examples.
the M-C algorithm achieves the same classification performance as traditional SVM with only a fraction of training examples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the M-C algorithm is an effective and practical way of eliminating the need for negative training examples in Web page classification.
the PEBL framework can significantly reduce the pre-processing work for Web page classification.
the PEBL framework is a viable alternative to traditional SVM for Web page classification.
